TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r1.claim: The owners called to one another in the morning to head to their crop if they meant to harvest it, then whispered together to prevent any poor person from entering the garden.

TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses their takhāfut as keeping their talk secret.

TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p175#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the sons set out after their father died, resolved to exclude the poor.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the owners' claim that they were lost as meaning they had lost the location of their garden.

NAHHAS:v5p9/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p9/r19.claim: An is accusative under an implied verb or an explanatory particle; antum is jussive under the condition, with the earlier verb serving as its answer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r5.claim: They were resolved to cut their crop that day.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r1.claim: Muqatil explains the orchard's crop as its fruit, grain, and grapes, which the heirs meant to harvest.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq takes صارمين to mean being determined to cut the palm trees' fruit.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the crop includes the garden's trees and plants, and the harvesters intend both grain harvest and a later stay for the date harvest because the seasons do not coincide.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p100#2/r4.claim: Here أن in أن اغدوا means that is or namely, as in another cited example.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r1.claim: They urge one another to go to the crop and cut its fruit.

JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r5.claim: Ṣarm is cutting, especially harvesting date fruit; ṣarām and jadhādh name the harvest, and the separation between companions is also called ṣarm.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195#2/r1.claim: Their ‘cultivation’ means fruits, crops, and grapes; صارمين means cutting the palm trees.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r2.claim: Readers among the Seven differ on whether the n in أن اغدوا is read with ḍamma or kasra.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r3.claim: صارمين can mean those harvesting their garden, or people resolutely carrying out their decision, like a decisive sword.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r6.claim: Their call was to set out early for their crop, meaning their cultivated plants and grapevines, if they intended to harvest the palms.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#4/r1.claim: Their ḥarth is the fruit, crops, and grapes, and ṣārimīn means those who cut the palms.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#3/r2.claim: The phrase says 'go upon' rather than 'go to' the harvest because they were approaching it in order to cut it; alternatively, ghada includes the sense of setting out toward it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r5.claim: They called one another early and told each other to set out for the crop; على implies approaching it or likens dawn harvest to an attacking force, and صرمين means reapers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#2/r1.claim: “Go early upon your harvest” uses “upon” because they approached to reap, or because go is given the sense of approaching; they intended to cut the crop.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p233/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p233/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p233/r1.claim: The date harvest is called ṣirām, the cutting or picking of palm dates.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r10.claim: صارمين apparently refers to cutting dates, though it may instead mean being resolved and determined, like a decisive sword.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains على as “upon” the crop because they intended to cut it, like an enemy coming upon people; it can also imply approaching early.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's assumption that غدا normally governs إلى, saying he knows it as taking على, as in a cited poem.

SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r1.claim: أن اغدوا may be a verbal noun clause reporting what they called out, or an explanatory clause because a speech-like verb precedes it.

SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says على حرثكم reflects going against the field to harvest it, or an implied sense of approaching; the author objects that غدا itself occurs with على.

SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r3.claim: The author notes direct poetic examples of غدا عليه and its synonym بكر عليه, so no special transitivity explanation is needed.

SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:22/r4.claim: The response to إن كنتم صارمين is omitted and understood as فاغدوا; صارمين means cutters and harvesters, or resolute in purpose like a sharp sword.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r1.claim: At daybreak they called one another to go harvest if they intended to reap the crop.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r2.claim: Mujahid says their crop was grapes.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r2.claim: They urged one another to go very early to their cultivated orchard, the place from which they expected benefit and which they regarded as theirs alone.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r3.claim: Calling themselves harvesters can mean those cutting the crop or those firmly resolved to cut it without sharing it.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r8.claim: Mujahid says their cultivated plot was a vineyard.

BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r7.claim: Their ‘harvest’ is the orchard and property, including crops and grape vines.

BURSEVI:v10p88/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88/r1.claim: Ḥarth can mean produce generally or crops specifically, essential human sustenance; ‘go upon’ conveys turning toward and taking possession.

BURSEVI:v10p88/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p88/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ḥarth as placing seed and preparing earth for planting; the planted land is also called ḥarth.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r1.claim: أن may explain the content of their calling, with اغدوا meaning go out, or it may be a verbal noun with an implied preposition; it can govern an imperative.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r2.claim: حرثكم means their orchard, and صارمين means intending to harvest the fruit.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r3.claim: The alternative that صارمين means decisive or resolute, by analogy with a sharp sword, is not persuasive.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r4.claim: Since غدا normally takes إلى, جار الله explains على through an included sense of turning toward and approaching the orchard.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r5.claim: Another explanation compares their dawn departure to an army advancing to seize something; the overlap in control and cutting yields a verbal metaphor or a representational metaphor.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#7/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan cites poetry showing غدا can take على and says بكر is its synonym.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r4.claim: Calling it their own cultivation assumes sole ownership; عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ evokes attacking and cutting it down as if striking an enemy.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.claim: They meant to finish the harvest completely and leave nothing for anyone, acting with extreme greed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r5.claim: إن كنتم صارمين is not a real condition but an impatient prod, as if delay meant they would miss that day's harvest; Ibn Umar used similar phrasing to urge al-Hajjaj at Arafat.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r6.claim: Ibn Umar told al-Hajjaj to proceed from Arafat at the proper time, saying that if he wanted the Sunna he should move on.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r7.claim: على حرثكم means reaching and settling at the orchard; alternatively غدا includes the sense of approaching, as in a line cited by al-Tibi about a whip and a serving bowl.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r8.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r8.claim: Al-Tibi cites the expression about a whip going out to fools and a bowl to the forbearing as a parallel construction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r9.claim: Harth literally means working soil to plant seeds or trees and remove weeds; here it means the garden maintained through cultivation.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r4.claim: They called to one another at daybreak to go early to the orchard and harvest if they were intent on cutting its fruit; aghdu means go early, with an implicit sense of approaching that explains ala rather than ila.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r3.claim: The term for cultivated land can denote the orchard because Arabian orchards included plots sown with crops, so both orchard and field vocabulary fit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r4.claim: Their call challenges the companions to set out immediately if they intend to harvest, warning that delay risks loss.

QIRAAT-ER:68:22:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:68:22:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:68:22:1#1/r1.claim: Ḍamma on nūn instead of kasra is a phonological variant before hamzat al-waṣl.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.claim: The brothers’ exclusion of the poor violated an ancient Near Eastern custom allowing the poor to glean and the Quranic command to give the harvest due on harvest day.
